catalog_quote: A phonological word consists of an obligatory nucleus plus optional onset and final peripheries. (See 5.3.) The nucleus is filled by a syllable which has an inherent toneme; the tones of the syllables which fill the peripheries depend on the tone which is on the nucleus of the word ... [5.2.1] Tone functions in the language of Nso as a feature of the syllable. There are eight phonemic tones in the language which can occur on nuclear syllables. The tones of the peripheral syllables are predictable from the tones of the nuclear syllables. ... The eight tonemes consist of: a) Three level tones: high, mid, low b) Two rising glides: high rising, low-high c) Three falling glides: high-mid, high-low, low falling ... [5.2.1.2] Peripheral syllables that fill the onset periphery of the word carry a low-falling tone if the tone on the nuclear syllable is low-falling. In all other cases they carry …

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: "Lam Nso nouns consist typically of a monosyllabic root and an optional prefix. ... When nouns are pronounced in isolation seven different tone patterns contrast on monosyllabic nouns ... These tone patterns occur at three pitch heights, high, mid and low. At each height a level tone contrasts with one that has a slight downglide ... The seventh tone pattern is a fall from high to low." TOC lists only segmental phonology, morphology, noun-class and tone chapters; no stress/accent section and no hit for stress/accent/promin in pp.7-30.

sources.quote: "Lamnso has a fairly complex tone system. According to Grebe (1984), there are three level tones, high, mid, and low, and four contour tones: high-mid, mid-low, high-low and low-falling. ... we do not mark tone. For a detailed description of the tonal system of Lamnso, see Grebe (1984) and Grebe & Grebe (1975)." No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the paper (a full-text search for stress/accent).
